Cc: Oliver Grant <ops-lead@evonix.ai>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightByte POC — coordinating global load window and handover

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We want to lock down the logistics for the POC load runs next week and hand the orchestration/runbook to your ops team for execution. A few asks up front so we can align schedules across our time zones (US west coast for BrightByte, EU for Evonix):

- Proposed primary window: Tue 2028-04-24 14:00–18:00 PDT (will be Wed morning in EU)
- Fallback window: Thu 2028-04-26 08:00–12:00 PDT
- Target throughput: start at 20k tokens/sec aggregate, ramp to 60k tokens/sec in 3 phases
- We will need the architecture deep-dive to be recorded and the runbook with clear abort criteria

Can your side confirm availability for the primary window and whether the suggested ramp plan looks feasible? Also please attach the latest runbook and an env matrix so our SREs can review dependencies.

Thanks,
Megan Li
Sr. ML Eng — BrightByte

Attachment: high-level-scope.pdf (1 page)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Megan Li <megan@brightbyte.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte POC — coordinating global load window and handover

Megan —

Appreciate the clear windows. Primary window (Tue 4/24 14:00–18:00 PDT) works for our ops team; I’ll block it tentatively. A few implementation notes from our side:

- We’ll own orchestration and the coordinated ramp. Suggest the following phases: 20k -> 40k -> 60k tokens/sec over ~45 minutes with 10–15 minute steady-state at each plateau.
- Abort criteria: sustained >3% error rate on generation endpoints for >5 minutes OR median p95 latency growth >2.5x baseline for >5 minutes.
- We need the runbook (please send) + a list of endpoints you expect to exercise.

I attached a revised runbook (runbook_v2.pdf) and an env-matrix.csv with the minimal infra variables we need populated. Can Aditya jump in on the latency targets and kernel/quantization notes?

—Jonas
Director, Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 8 pages); env-matrix.csv (CSV, 1 file)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Megan Li <megan@brightbyte.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-20T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte POC — coordinating global load window and handover

On Thu, Apr 19, 2028 at 10:03 AM jonas_weber@redwood.ai wrote:
> I attached a revised runbook (runbook_v2.pdf) and an env-matrix.csv with the minimal infra variables we need populated.

Thanks — quick technical follow-up from the runtime/serving side:

- Kernel selection: for the model you shared, we expect two viable execution variants (fp16 + int8-ql4). For the ramp I recommend starting on fp16 for baseline correctness then switch to int8-ql4 at the 40k step to cut GPU token cost; we’ll monitor quality metrics.
- KV cache sizing: set max_cache_tokens to 1024 for the long-tail dialogs you mentioned; otherwise we’ll see memory pressure at 60k aggregate.
- Batching policy: use adaptive continuous batching with a 15ms batching window during steady-state; lower to 5ms during ramp transitions.
- Throughput verification: we’ll report token/sec (aggregate), median/p95 latency for generation calls, and the model-side tail latency for KV lookups.

I’m adding suggested latency targets into throughput-profiles.md and attaching it here. Please confirm if BrightByte can provide a small validation corpus (500 prompts) by Monday so we can run pre-checks.

Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: throughput-profiles.md (Markdown, 3 pages)
From: Megan Li <megan@brightbyte.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ops-lead@evonix.ai

- We can deliver a 500-prompt validation corpus by Mon 2028-04-22 09:00 PDT and provide a short list of the exact endpoints we’ll exercise.
- Primary window still preferred (Tue 4/24). Evonix (Oliver) will be on-call for model infra in EU.
- We’d like to record the architecture deep-dive and have the runbook show the exact sequence for fallback to a smaller model variant (e.g., ql4 -> fp16 downgrade) if quality drops.

Also, can we add a short security sync (15m) before the run to confirm audit/log capture and data retention settings? Oliver — can you confirm availability for Tue 4/24 11:30 PDT / 20:30 CEST for that call?

Best,
Megan
